headline: Large User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates that large energy users, such as data centers, bear a greater share of the costs for new grid infrastructure and capacity, reducing the burden on residential ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor Spanberger.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial users.
news_headline: Virginia Legislature Bucks Governor's Amendments to Dominion-Backed Bill
news_summary: This article discusses a bill, supported by Dominion Energy, that assigns certain electric grid upgrade costs to data centers. It highlights how the legislature rejected some of Governor Spanberger's cost-saving amendments, but the core intent of shifting costs to data centers remains, leading to increased bills for data centers and potential savings for residential customers.

headline: Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates that water utilities report the total volume of water provided to data centers, enhancing transparency and providing data for water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservationists, Virginia League of Conservation Voters.
news_headline: New Virginia law requires data center water usage be made public
news_summary: This article details the new Virginia law, SB 553, which requires local water authorities to report data center water usage. The aim is to provide transparency and inform future water management decisions, with the data expected to be publicly available by January 1, 2027.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new large data centers, including noise profiles on nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates, Delegate Sam Rasoul.
news_headline: Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: This article discusses HB 153, a new Virginia law that took effect July 1, 2026, requiring developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise impacts on nearby homes and schools. While it mandates studies and disclosures, it does not set specific noise limits or water caps.
